issues.legal_issue: A prior decision allowing a party to claim the benefit of a statutory provision does not bar a later dispute over the provision’s interpretation when that interpretation was not decided earlier.
material_facts: In an earlier appeal concerning execution, the Federal Court held that the judgment-debtors could claim the benefit of the later enactment when the executing court assessed property for sale.
The earlier appeal did not determine the correct interpretation of the provision governing the calculation of interest.
The judgment-debtors later argued in the execution proceedings that the earlier decision barred the decree-holder from disputing their interpretation.
issues.conclusion: The doctrine of constructive res judicata did not bar the decree-holder from contesting the judgment-debtors’ interpretation because the earlier decision had not decided that issue.
issues.legal_principle: Constructive res judicata does not apply to an issue that was not directly or constructively in issue and decided in the earlier proceeding. The earlier Federal Court decision, Ramnandan Prasad Narain Singh v. Kulpati Shri Mahanth Goshwami Madhwanand Ramji ([1940] F.C.R. 1), decided that the judgment-debtors could claim the statutory benefit, not how the relevant provision should be interpreted.

predicates.execution_proceeding: The current dispute arose in proceedings to execute a money decree.
predicates.prior_decision_recognized_statutory_bene: An earlier decision allowed a party to claim the benefit of a statutory provision.
predicates.prior_decision_did_not_determine_interpr: The earlier decision did not determine the interpretation now disputed.
predicates.later_interpretation_challenge_is_not_ba: The later dispute over the provision’s interpretation is not barred by constructive res judicata.

issues.definition: When an execution proceeding follows an earlier decision that recognized a statutory benefit but did not determine the disputed interpretation, the later interpretation challenge is not barred by constructive res judicata.

issues.legal_issue: When a debt is renewed in a later document and the claim is based on that renewed debt, the later document determines the loan amount used to cap pre-suit interest.
material_facts: The debt originated in an earlier loan and was represented through successive renewed documents that included accrued interest in the amounts recorded.
A later mortgage document recorded the renewed debt, and the judgment-debtors disputed whether the interest limit should instead be calculated from the amount of the original loan.
The dispute arose in execution proceedings in which the statutory calculation was relevant to assessing the secured properties.
issues.conclusion: For the interest limit, the loan amount is the amount mentioned in or evidenced by the later document, not the amount advanced under the original loan. Interest for the period before suit, together with interest already realised after the later document, cannot exceed the loan amount in that later document.
issues.legal_principle: Section 7 of the Bihar Money-lenders (Regulation of Transactions) Act, 1939, limits pre-suit interest by reference to the loan advanced or, where the loan is based on a document, the amount mentioned in or evidenced by that document. The relevant document is the final document on which the claim is based, rather than the original loan document. The Court relied on the consistent Patna High Court construction in Singheshwar Singh v. Madni Prasad Singh (A.I.R. 1940 Pat. 65), Lal Singh v. Ramnarain Ram (A.I.R. 1942 Pat. 138), Madho Prasad Singh v. Mukutdhari Singh (193 I.C. 661), and the Full Bench decision in Deo Nandan Prasad v. Ram Prasad (I.L.R. 23 Pat. 618), which distinguished section 7 from section 8. It also referred to Surendra Prasad Narain Singh v. Sri Gajadhar Prasad Sahu Trust Estate ([1940] F.C.R. 39), noting the provision’s obscurity and the Legislature’s acquiescence in the established construction.

predicates.execution_proceeding: The dispute arises in proceedings to execute a money decree and assess property for sale.
predicates.debt_renewed_in_later_document: The outstanding debt is recorded in a later document that renews an earlier loan.
predicates.claim_based_on_later_document: The claim for which the interest limit is calculated is based on the later document.
predicates.interest_cap_is_measured_by_amount_in_la: The interest limit is calculated by reference to the loan amount stated or evidenced in the later document.

issues.definition: When an execution proceeding concerns a debt renewed in a later document and the claim is based on that document, the interest cap is measured by the amount in the later document.
